changes.catalogueSays: commercial-code 30 حرية الإثبات في المواد التجارية (الفواتير، الدفاتر، المراسلات)
changes.reason: The article lists the means that prove a commercial contract rather than an unlimited freedom: the invoice proves only when accepted [commercial-code 30 ¶4], and witnesses or any other means only if the court decides to accept them [commercial-code 30 ¶7]; deeds, letters and books are [commercial-code 30 ¶2], [commercial-code 30 ¶3], [commercial-code 30 ¶5], [commercial-code 30 ¶6].
[civil-code 106 ¶1] says the contract is the law of the parties; the formal-notice module already carries it, so it is imported.
[civil-code 164 ¶1] compels the debtor to perform in kind, where possible, after notice under articles 180 and 181; imported from the formal-notice module with its prior step.

changes.catalogueSays: civil-code 176 التعويض عن عدم التنفيذ أو التأخر
changes.reason: [civil-code 176 ¶1] gives damages for non-performance unless the impossibility arose from a cause outside the debtor's control, and the same for delay; imported from the formal-notice module.

changes.catalogueSays: civil-code 179 لا يستحق التعويض إلا بعد إعذار المدين
changes.reason: [civil-code 179 ¶1] makes compensation due only after notice, unless a text provides otherwise; imported with the module's prior step and its exemptions.

changes.catalogueSays: إلزام المدعى عليها بأن تؤدي للمدعية مبلغ (...) دج قيمة الفواتير غير المسددة
changes.reason: Rests on the binding contract and its performance in good faith [civil-code 106 ¶1], [civil-code 107 ¶1], and the price falling due at delivery [civil-code 388 ¶1].

changes.catalogueSays: إلزام المدعى عليها بتعويض قدره (...) دج عن التأخر في الوفاء
changes.reason: Rests on damages for delay [civil-code 176 ¶1] and [civil-code 186 ¶1], assessed under [civil-code 182 ¶1] and [civil-code 182 ¶2], and due only after notice [civil-code 179 ¶1]; whether article 186 reaches companies is open point o2.
An accepted invoice proves the commercial contract [commercial-code 30 ¶4]; the document name now asks for proof of acceptance.
Purchase orders and delivery notes are private deeds, and correspondence is letters, both means of proof of a commercial contract [commercial-code 30 ¶3], [commercial-code 30 ¶5].
The parties' books prove a commercial contract [commercial-code 30 ¶6], and traders' books are evidence against those traders [civil-code 330 ¶2].

Imported from the formal-notice module, which lists the notice itself and the bailiff's service record or acknowledgement of receipt, required only when a notice was served; notice is given by a warning or an act standing in its place [civil-code 180 ¶1].

No text in the store requires it; it is kept as a supporting document because trader status governs the proof rules [civil-code 333 ¶1] and the section [cpca 531 ¶1]; the register's own articles were requested.
The contract is made by matching wills [civil-code 59 ¶1] and proved by the means of [commercial-code 30 ¶1]; its commercial character rests on articles not in the store (open point o1).
Delivery makes the price due [civil-code 388 ¶1]; it is proved by deeds and accepted invoices [commercial-code 30 ¶3], [commercial-code 30 ¶4].

The creditor proves the obligation and the debtor his release [civil-code 323 ¶1]; the price is due at delivery and paid where the thing is delivered unless agreed otherwise [civil-code 388 ¶1], [civil-code 387 ¶1].
Notice precedes compelled performance and damages [civil-code 164 ¶1], [civil-code 179 ¶1], and is made as [civil-code 180 ¶1] says; the step itself is imported.

changes.catalogueSays: لا يستحق التعويض إلا بعد إعذار المدين
changes.reason: [civil-code 179 ¶1], with the exemptions of [civil-code 181 ¶2] to [civil-code 181 ¶5] and the agreed default of [civil-code 180 ¶1], is the imported module's prior step; it warns and never blocks.

The seller's right to a price supplement for excess quantity falls by limitation one year after actual delivery [civil-code 366 ¶1], counted under [civil-code 314 ¶1] and pleaded only by the debtor [civil-code 321 ¶1]; a limitation, so it only warns.
The general and short limitations are imported from the periods module: [civil-code 308 ¶1], [civil-code 312 ¶2], [civil-code 309 ¶1], with the start at the due date [civil-code 315 ¶1].

The commercial section hears commercial disputes not given to the specialised commercial court [cpca 531 ¶1]; cases are listed by nature [cpca 32 ¶4] and a court without sections sends them to the civil section [cpca 32 ¶5]; the mixed act is open point o4.
Supplies by a trader to a person who does not trade in them are time-barred after one year [civil-code 312 ¶2], and traders' books are not evidence against non-traders [civil-code 330 ¶1].
The buyer's warranty action against defects is a different claim with its own one-year limitation from delivery [civil-code 383 ¶1].
Outside commercial matters, acts above the threshold may not be proved by witnesses [civil-code 333 ¶1], while [commercial-code 30 ¶1] governs only commercial contracts.
The notice, its means, its exemptions and its date before the petition are the formal-notice module's [civil-code 180 ¶1], [civil-code 181 ¶1].
Counting, start, interruption and pleading of limitation, and the burden of proof, are the periods module's [civil-code 314 ¶1], [civil-code 317 ¶1], [civil-code 321 ¶1], [civil-code 323 ¶1].
The administrative courts [cpca 800 ¶2], the specialised commercial court [cpca 536 مكرر ¶1] and the order to pay [cpca 306 ¶1] take some of these debts out of the commercial section.
Statements on which the claim's own section rule rests: [cpca 32 ¶4], [cpca 32 ¶5], [cpca 531 ¶1], [cpca 532 ¶1].
The defendant's domicile [cpca 37 ¶1], the supply and commercial-matter options [cpca 39 ¶4], [cpca 39 ¶5], and the jurisdiction clause valid only between traders [cpca 45 ¶1].

A claim in the specialised commercial court's matters follows a conciliation whose failure record is attached on pain of formal inadmissibility [cpca 536 مكرر 4 ¶1], [cpca 536 مكرر 4 ¶3]; none is required before the commercial section.
The petition's mandatory particulars, the legal person's details among them [cpca 15 ¶1], [cpca 15 ¶5], standing and interest [cpca 13 ¶1], and the Arabic language [cpca 8 ¶1].
Provisional execution when judgment rests on an official deed or an acknowledged promise [cpca 323 ¶2], or in urgency [cpca 323 ¶3].
The losing party bears the costs [cpca 419 ¶1].
The buyer pays more when the quantity delivered exceeds the contract and the price is per unit [civil-code 365 ¶2], within the year of [civil-code 366 ¶1].
A written contract or framework agreement, if any, proves the commercial contract as an official or private deed [commercial-code 30 ¶2], [commercial-code 30 ¶3].
Statements for the elements: good-faith performance [civil-code 107 ¶1], formation [civil-code 59 ¶1], the price due at delivery [civil-code 388 ¶1] and the place of payment [civil-code 387 ¶1].
Statements on proof: traders' books against traders [civil-code 330 ¶2] and not against non-traders [civil-code 330 ¶1], and the witness threshold outside commercial matters [civil-code 333 ¶1].
Statements on the measure of damages: loss and lost gain [civil-code 182 ¶1], limited to foreseeable harm in contract absent fraud or gross fault [civil-code 182 ¶2].
Statements for d1, n1 and n2: [civil-code 365 ¶2], [civil-code 366 ¶1], [civil-code 383 ¶1], [civil-code 312 ¶2], [civil-code 314 ¶1], [civil-code 321 ¶1].
